Commentary.Commentary: 2-0 up then, go the West Indies, with a game to go. Will we expect the bench to play a part in the third game? Or is the fruit of a whitewash too hard to ignore? What can Afghanistan do to avoid a whitewash? Batted first, lost. Bowled first, lost again. Probably, the absence of pressure in the third game might just help them to do well, whatever they do. Join us on Monday, 11th November, 2019 at 2 pm local (0830 GMT) for all The action from the final ODI at this same venue. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

NICHOLAS POORAN HAS BEEN ADJUDGED THE MAN OF THE MATCH for his flamboyant innings. Thanks the almighty for giving him the opportunity to play well here. On his innings, Pooran says that he just stuck to his basics and then concentrated on playing his strokes. Promises that there is definitely more to come from him in future.

Victorious West Indies skipper, Kieron Pollard smiles on the reminder that West Indies have finally won an ODI series after 5 years. Praises his team for sticking to the plans which were laid out when they set foot from the Caribbean. On the pitch, Pollard says that it was on the slower side and they believed it will turn in the evening. Praises the openers for setting up a fine platform, though also admits that there was a collapse in the middle order. Wants to celebrate with the guys and soak in the atmosphere. Stresses that winning is a habit and they would like to keep winning. On the flies while playing, Kieron says that he has never played in such an environment and stresses that health too, is equally important. Hopes that in the final game, there are no such insects.

Afghanistan captain, Rashid Khan, feels that his team started well with the ball in the first 40 overs but then the momentum got snatched away. Praises Pooran for his knock. Although, he says that 248 was chaseable on this wicket, given the line-up that they have. On his bowling plans, in spite of the strong opening stand, Rashid says that the plan was to only keep bowling dots and wait for the batsmen to commit mistakes, which eventually happened, due to the sustained pressure. Lauds Najibullah and Nabi for putting their hands up but laments about his team not finishing off the job, which was the case in the first ODI as well. On the plans to break their losing rut in ODIs, Khan says that the focus only has to be on playing positive cricket and believing in themselves, as he adds that once that happens, they can get back to winning ways.

248 to chase. With dew present. Easy? Should have been. But it wasn't. Afghanistan never got set in this chase and struggled to cope with the slowing track. Only Najibullah Zadran crossed 50 while the next highest scorer was Rahmat with 33. Sheldon Cottrell did the damage with the new ball, keeping the pressure uptight and finishing with 3 wickets overall. But how good was Roston Chase? His 3/30 in 10 overs was what choked Afghanistan and they could not find a way. Hayden Walsh then cleaned up the tail with a 3-fer, which also included the wicket of Nabi (albeit a lucky one). Please stay tuned for the presentation...

2 matches, 2 different types of victories for West Indies. In the first game, Afghanistan were told to be unlucky, because dew hampered them in the second innings. If that was the case, what can be told about this game? Without a doubt, the pitch was difficult to bat on in the first innings but the Windies batted really well. Hope and Lewis played sensibly, not trying to go too hard and their 98-run opening stand set the platform. There was a collapse thereon but Nicholas Pooran's 67 took the 'visitors' close to 250, which looked to be a competitive total. And by and large, it indeed was.
At last. An ODI series win for West Indies. August 2014 was the last time when the Men from the Caribbean tasted a series victory in this format. Boy, has it been a long time coming.

OUT! LBW! Or shall we say, adjudged LBW? Because Nabi is not happy at all. He is walking off, shaking his head and hitting the ground with his bat in frustration. No reviews in this series, remember. Hard to see how that can be out. 1. It is a leg spinner. 2. Nabi got down and across his stumps and one could see two-and-a-half sticks when he attempted that paddle shot. Which means, that when he attempted the stroke, the impact could have been outside off. 3. Given that it is a leggie, couldn't it have been turning away? West Indies won't care. They are 3 wickets away from winning their first ODI series in 5 years...

On a length on middle, Zazai flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! Zazai makes good use of the Free Hit. Short of a length delivery, Zazai pulls it over mid-wicket for a maximum. That was a very good shot from him.
Free Hit coming up!
NO BALL! Holder has overstepped. On a length on middle, Shah flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
On a good length on off, Rahmat defends it off the back foot.
BEATEN! On a good length  and outside off, Zazai looks to swing at this one but misses it.
On a good length on leg, Zazai looks to flick but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Full delivery on off, Rahmat drives it towards covers for a single.
On a length on off, Shah plays it to covers.
On a good length on off, Rahmat plays it to point.
Good length delivery on off, Rahmat defends it out.
On a good length on leg, Zazai looks to flick but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Full delivery on off, Zazai drives it to mid off.
FOUR! That has taken the top edge. A short ball, around off, Zazai looks to pull but there is extra bounce on that one. The ball takes the top edge and flies over the keeper to the fine leg fence.
Length delivery outside off, Shah guides it towards third man for a single.
On a length on off, Rahmat plays it to point.
On a good length and outside off, Shah shoulders arms to this one.
Full delivery on leg, Zazai looks to flick but gets hit on the pads.
Length delivery on off, Shah dabs it towards third man for a run.
FOUR! Second boundary of the over. On a length and outside off, Rahmat drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
On a good length on middle, Shah keeps it out.
FOUR! Nice shot. Full delivery outside off, Shah drives it through point where the fielder dives and tries to stop it but it goes through him for a boundary.
Good length delivery on off, Shah defends it off the back foot.
Short delivery on middle, Shah pulls it over mid-wicket. Hetmyer chases it and does well to pull it back before the ropes. The batsmen get three runs.
FOUR! Nice shot. Short delivery on middle, Shah pulls it over fine leg for a boundary.
On a good length on middle, Rahmat keeps it out.
Good length delivery on off, Shah defends it out.
On a good length on off, Rahmat defends it off the back foot.
Short of a length delivery on leg, Zazai pulls it towards square leg for a run.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Landed around off on a good length, Shah defends it out.
Huge appeal this time but it is turned down. Full ball on the pads, Shah looks to flick but misses out.

Dropped! That should've been taken easily but that is not the case. Joseph has spilled the easiest of chances. This is a short of a length ball outside off, Zazai goes for the pull but gets a top edge which goes high towards square leg. Joseph gets under the ball but makes a mess of it. A single is taken.
Zazai this time swings hard but misses out. Length ball outside off, Zazai drives but misses.
Full ball on off, pushed towards mid off by Zazai this time.
Full around off, tapped towards point. Just a single from this over.
On middle, blocked onto the pitch.
In the channel outside off, Shah shoulders arms.
Shortish length ball outside off, Rahmat blocks it off the front foot towards point.
Good length ball on middle, tucked towards mid-wicket for a quick single. There is a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Could've been a risky run that one.
Good length ball around off, Zazai blocks it off the back foot.
Jason Holder to bowl from the other end.
Outside off, Shah leaves it alone.
Rahmat Shah is the new batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Early setback for Afghanistan in the chase. Cottrell bowls it back of a length and on middle, Ahmadi looks to break the shackles but is not in a position to play the pull. He gets a top edge on it and it goes to Sheldon Cottrell who moves to his right and takes a comfortable catch.
Fuller one on the pads, Ahmadi flicks it to square leg.

An appeal but Ahmadi is lucky to get an inside edge on this one. A typical left arm bowler's delivery pitching on off and getting back into the batsman. Ahmadi does well to get his bat down in time. Cottrell appeals, but only for the umpire to shake his head.
On a good length, around off, Ahmadi defends it to covers.
Afghanistan are underway! Length and on off, Zazai pushes it to the mid-wicket region and gets off the mark.

Welcome back for the chase. West Indies players are out on the field taking their respective fielding positions. Out come the two Afghanistan openers, Hazratullah Zazai and Javed Ahmadi. Sheldon Cottrell to start the proceedings with the ball.
